approachQuestion.prompt:
Each of n labels is a nonempty sequence of symbols in [0,W-1]. Pick two different label indices having no symbol in common and maximize the product of their lengths. Return zero if no such pair exists. Repeated symbols inside a label count toward its length.

Constraints: 2 <= n <= 5000; 1 <= W <= 64; label lengths are at most W.
Example: W=8, labels=[[0,1],[2,2,3],[1,4]] -> 6. Edge case: labels=[[0],[0]] -> 0.

Choose the best approach under these constraints.
constraints: W is a width parameter; one W-bit mask operation costs constant time. Let L be the total number of symbols. Products and lengths fit in one machine word.
Inputs are read-only. Include all temporary storage and any call stack; exclude the supplied input and the returned output. No input copy is implicit.

options.text: Build a symbol-presence mask per label. Examine every unordered label pair; if their masks AND to zero, update the best length product.
options.feedback: A set bit captures presence independently of repetitions. Zero intersection is exactly the no-shared-symbol condition.

options.text: For every label pair compare all symbol occurrences across the two labels to detect any match, then update the product when none matches.
options.feedback: This is correct for every label, but repeats symbol comparisons that can be summarized in one presence mask.

options.text: Build presence masks and accept a label pair whenever their XOR is nonzero.
options.feedback: Different masks may still overlap: [0,1] and [1,2] have nonzero XOR but share symbol 1.

options.text: Deduplicate symbols inside each label and maximize the product of distinct-symbol counts.
options.feedback: Presence controls compatibility, but the objective uses original lengths. [0,0] and [1,1,1] have product 6, not 1.

feedback.reason: A label's mask records membership, while its original length remains separate because repetitions still affect the product.
details: Summarize each label by a word whose set bits denote symbols appearing in it, keeping the original length separately. Test every unordered pair with AND and maximize the product only when their intersection is empty.

A label's mask records membership, while its original length remains separate because repetitions still affect the product. Zero AND proves disjoint symbol sets; equal masks do not mean equal lengths.

feedback.reason: Read L symbols, then test every unordered label pair with word operations.
details: Mask construction visits L symbols. The prescribed comparison phase always visits all pairs and each test uses constant word operations. One mask and length per label occupy O(n) words.

“O(n²W²) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: This describes repeated cross-label symbol comparisons, not precomputed masks.
“O(L+n²) time, O(nW) auxiliary space”: Each label uses one packed mask, not W separate cells.
“O(L+n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: The stated method still enumerates every unordered label pair.
